why_this_tool: Amazon SageMaker offers shadow tests, blue/green traffic shifting with canary, linear and all-at-once modes, rolling updates and alarm-driven automatic rollback as managed endpoint features, so every strategy in this lesson can be practised against one endpoint.
alternatives: Argo Rollouts drives canary and blue/green steps on Kubernetes with metric analysis from Prometheus; Istio provides the traffic splitting and mirroring underneath such rollouts; KServe gives a canary traffic percentage per inference service on your own cluster; Seldon Core adds shadow and experiment routing on Kubernetes; Amazon CloudWatch is not a rollout tool but supplies the alarms that gate a SageMaker rollout.

setup.do: Read the pricing section and plan every exercise on the smallest CPU instance type, since SageMaker endpoints need a paid AWS account and have no laptop mode; the closest local substitute is drafting and validating each request file with the AWS CLI skeleton option before sending it.
setup.done_when: You have written down the instance type you will use, a spending limit, and the list of resources to delete after each session.

source.title: What is Amazon SageMaker AI? - Amazon SageMaker AI

setup.why: Endpoints bill for as long as they exist, and blue/green updates briefly run two fleets. Knowing the cost model up front lets you keep the practice cheap and delete resources on time.

setup.do: Configure AWS security credentials on the laptop for a non-root identity allowed to manage SageMaker endpoints, CloudWatch alarms and EventBridge rules.
setup.done_when: An AWS CLI identity check from the laptop returns your non-root user or role.

source.title: AWS General Reference - AWS General Reference

setup.why: Every later step calls the SageMaker API from your laptop. Scoped credentials are also what a deployment pipeline would use.

setup.do: Create a baseline real-time endpoint from a small CPU model and one endpoint configuration; this is the champion that every rollout will update.
setup.done_when: The endpoint shows the status InService and answers a test invocation.
setup.why: Deployment guardrails only apply to updates of an existing endpoint that is in service. You need a stable starting fleet to shift traffic away from.

setup.do: Create the canary prerequisites: a second endpoint configuration for the new model version and at least one CloudWatch alarm on the endpoint, such as error count or latency.
setup.done_when: Two endpoint configurations exist and the alarm is listed in the OK state.

source.title: Use canary traffic shifting - Amazon SageMaker AI

setup.why: The alarm is the automated check that decides whether a rollout continues or rolls back. Without it a staged rollout is only a slow deployment.

steps.do: Query the baseline endpoint with DescribeEndpoint and identify the production variants, the endpoint configuration name, the status and the last deployment configuration fields.
steps.done_when: You can point to the variant name, its current weight and instance count, and the endpoint status in the response.
steps.why: These response fields are the object model you will watch during every rollout. Reading them on a quiet endpoint makes the later changes easy to spot.

steps.do: Create an EventBridge rule that matches the model package state change event, so that approving a new model version is the recorded trigger for starting a rollout.
steps.done_when: Changing the approval status of a model package produces a matching event at the rule target, such as a log group.

source.title: Events that Amazon SageMaker AI sends to Amazon EventBridge - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: Promotion and rollout should be linked: a version gets approved first and only then exposed to traffic. The event gives you an auditable hand-off between the two.

steps.do: Create a shadow test in the console that adds the new model as a shadow variant and copies a percentage of live requests to it, on a paid CPU endpoint as there is no laptop mode.
steps.done_when: The shadow test is running and its dashboard shows latency and error metrics for the production and shadow variants side by side, while callers still receive only production responses.

source.title: Create a shadow test - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: A shadow variant sees real inputs but its responses are never returned to callers. It is the lowest-risk way to check latency and errors under production conditions.

steps.do: Configure an all-at-once blue/green update to the new endpoint configuration with a baking period and your alarm in the auto rollback configuration.
steps.done_when: The endpoint goes through Updating to InService on the new configuration, and the old fleet is terminated only after the baking period ends.

source.title: Use all at once traffic shifting - Amazon SageMaker AI

verified.section_found: Configure All At Once Traffic Shifting

steps.why: This is the simplest blue/green form: a full new fleet, one traffic switch, then a watch period before the old fleet is removed. It teaches the baking period and termination wait before you add stepwise shifting.

steps.do: Run a canary traffic shifting update from the CLI that sends a small canary of capacity to the green fleet, waits, then shifts the remainder.
steps.done_when: DescribeEndpoint shows the canary settings in the deployment configuration, and the endpoint finishes InService on the new configuration after the wait interval.

source.title: Use canary traffic shifting - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: Canary limits the blast radius of a bad version to a small share of traffic. It is the managed counterpart of a canary release with a Kubernetes rollout controller.

steps.do: Configure a linear traffic shifting update with a fixed step size and wait interval, then compare how long it takes against the canary run.
steps.done_when: You have noted the total rollout time and number of traffic steps for the linear and the canary run.

source.title: Use linear traffic shifting - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: Linear shifting gives more checkpoints than canary at the cost of a longer rollout. Timing both lets you choose a mode per model with evidence.

steps.do: Configure a rolling deployment with a rolling batch size and a rollback batch size on an endpoint with at least two instances.
steps.done_when: The update completes batch by batch and the endpoint returns to InService without the instance count ever doubling.

source.title: Use rolling deployments - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: Rolling updates replace capacity in batches instead of doubling the fleet. That matters when quota or cost rules out a full blue/green fleet.

steps.do: Reproduce a failed rollout by forcing your alarm into the alarm state during a baking period and watching the automatic rollback.
steps.done_when: The endpoint returns to InService on the previous configuration, and you have recorded the time from alarm to full recovery.

source.title: Use rolling deployments - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: A rollback you have never triggered is not a rollback plan. Rehearsing shows how long recovery takes and what the endpoint reports while it happens.

steps.do: Write the canary update as a script using the SageMaker Python SDK in a pinned environment, taking the endpoint name and new configuration name as inputs.
steps.done_when: Running the script twice from a clean environment performs the same canary update both times with no manual edits.
steps.why: A rollout typed by hand cannot be reviewed or repeated. A pinned, parameterised script is what a pipeline job runs for every release.

steps.do: Run a champion/challenger experiment by configuring two production variants with traffic weights, then compare their per-variant metrics alongside a business outcome you log yourself.
steps.done_when: Per-variant invocation counts match the configured weights, and you can name the winning variant from your logged outcome.

source.title: Validation of models in production - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: Shadow and canary answer whether the new version is safe; an online experiment answers whether it is better. Splitting real responses between variants is the only way to measure outcomes.

steps.do: Create an EventBridge rule on the endpoint deployment state change event and route it to a notification target.
steps.done_when: A rehearsed rollback produces a notification that shows the deployment state transitions.

source.title: Events that Amazon SageMaker AI sends to Amazon EventBridge - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: On-call engineers need to learn about a rollback from an alert, not by polling the endpoint. The event also gives a timeline for post-incident review.

steps.do: Deploy a full production-like release by chaining the pieces: approval event, shadow test, scripted canary update gated by alarms with auto rollback, and deployment state notifications; then delete all endpoints.
steps.done_when: One approved model version reaches full traffic with no manual step after approval, a second deliberately bad version is rolled back automatically, and no endpoints remain afterwards.

source.title: Deployment guardrails for updating models in production - Amazon SageMaker AI

steps.why: Each strategy covers a different risk, and in production they run as one sequence with automated gates. Running the chain end to end shows where the hand-offs can fail.
